brief: GS midday US equities color, 1 Oct 2026. Equities rally into the close (NDX, then RTY, then SPX) as yields cool and WTI retreats, with the equal-weight S&P reversing September's historic cap-weight-vs-equal-weight dispersion by outperforming the cap-weighted index intraday. Accenture jumps 18%, its largest one-day gain on record, beating heavily bearish expectations against a short setup, lifting the broader IT services group. The credit desk flags four points: spreads sit at historical tights but, roll-adjusted, are back at July's wides; issuance stays heavy despite higher rates, which combined with weak performance of recent large deals is causing indigestion; quality is diverging within high yield, concentrated in consumer-exposed levered names; and the cross-asset desk sees rising interest in credit as a macro hedge. Amazon is added to GIR's conviction list, up 8% YTD, trailing only Microsoft among megacaps; the price target rises to $375 on AWS strength and AI-driven margin upside. Flow desk notes ETFs at 32% of tape, SPX CTA levels, the floor net better-to-buy, long-onlys mixed, hedge funds net buyers. Chart of the day: the 10-year's break above 5% this month has driven a surge in fixed income ETF trading volume.
